lines.trans: Why didn't you tell the truth right away?
I was very ashamed to admit it, Kostya.
Move in with me into a big apartment.
How many rooms are in your apartment?
I have two separate rooms.
Will we pay for the apartment fifty-fifty?
Yes, each pays exactly half the amount.
And does Nastya come over to you often?
She does not come, we are not dating.
So there is no serious relationship between you?
We are simply good friends and colleagues.
Then I gladly agree to move in!
Great, this evening I expect your things.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

встречаться.gloss: to meet; to date, to go out

meanings.en: to date, to go out (with someone)

examples.trans: We've been dating for a month.
We've been going out for a month already.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: also a flat number in an address

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: professional associate (common gender, declined like feminine)

examples.text: Мой коллега помог мне с отчётом.
examples.trans: My colleague helped me with the report.

meanings.note: meжду нами = between us; между прочим = by the way, for your information

examples.trans: For your information, I am the chairman of the court.
You two sort it out between yourselves here.

между.governs: instrumental (or genitive in a few set phrases)

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дельный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('separate').

examples.text: У меня есть отдельная комната в коммуналке.
examples.trans: I have a separate room in a communal flat.

examples.text: У меня есть две отдельные комнаты.

meanings.note: used as an exclamation of approval

examples.trans: I know this town really well!

examples.text: А я испорчу отношения с будущим мэром.
examples.trans: And I'll ruin my relationship with the future mayor.
We have a very warm relationship.

examples.text: Ты с ума сошёл? У нас с тобой только деловые отношения!
examples.trans: Have you lost your mind? Between you and me it's strictly business!
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

переезжать.gloss: to move (house), to relocate; to cross

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.

examples.text: Переезжай ко мне в большую квартиру.
examples.trans: Move in with me into a big apartment.

переехать.gloss: to move (to a new home or city)

examples.trans: They moved into a new flat.

examples.text: Ты в Москву переехала, да? Поедем сейчас в сауну, посидим!
examples.trans: You moved to Moscow, right? Let's go to a sauna now and sit for a while!

meanings.note: платить за + accusative = to pay for

examples.text: А вашу работу вернуть можно. И мы хорошо платим.
examples.trans: But we can get your job back for you. And we pay well.
Three and a half per mille?

examples.text: Три с половиной промилле? У меня семь кредитов!
examples.trans: Three and a half per mille? I have seven loans!

пополам.gloss: in half, fifty-fifty, equally between two

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'полам').

examples.trans: And we'll split the money fifty-fifty!
We split the bill in half.

examples.text: Я за комнаткой пригляжу. Может, сдам кому, а денежки пополам!
examples.trans: I'll look after the little room. Maybe I'll rent it to someone, and we'll split the money!
Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

examples.text: Никак, я тебя на понт взяла. А ты сейчас сама призналась.
examples.trans: No way at all, I called your bluff. And you just confessed yourself.

meanings.note: regularly, or as a general invitation: приходи!

examples.trans: If you change your mind, come back. The job is waiting.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

examples.text: Он бы сейчас до потолка прыгал от радости.
examples.trans: He would be jumping to the ceiling for joy right now.
What a joy to see you!

examples.text: Мы с радостью сообщаем вам новость. Ваш долг полностью аннулирован!
examples.trans: We gladly inform you of the news. Your debt is completely canceled!

meanings.note: ironic: Сталину расскажите = tell that to Stalin
ровно десять секунд = exactly ten seconds

examples.trans: Like a real man, exactly ten seconds.
They cut it exactly in half.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

examples.text: Я приехала к очень серьёзному человеку.
examples.trans: I have come to see a very important man.

examples.text: Я приехала к очень серьёзному человеку. Он меня ждёт.
examples.trans: I have come to see a very important man. He is waiting for me.

meanings.note: almost always the short form: я согласен (man), я согласна (woman)
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'умма'). Common feminine noun meaning 'sum, amount' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: О, это, Аркашенька, бывает очень часто.
examples.trans: Oh, that happens very often, Arkashenka.
We often meet in the park.
I used to come see you often.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
